scenes.visual: Title card: One Question for Every Number

scenes.tts: The original Neuropixels probe carries nine hundred sixty recording sites. Does it record nine hundred sixty neurons?
scenes.caption: The original Neuropixels probe carries 960 recording sites. Does it record 960 neurons?
scenes.visual: A thin silicon shank fills the frame; 960 small sites light up along it, with the number 960 on screen. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: The original Neuropixels probe carries 960 recording sites. Does it record 960 neurons?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Not necessarily. The original probe reads out only three hundred eighty four sites at a time. Each one read out is a channel.
scenes.caption: Not necessarily. The original probe reads out only 384 sites at a time. Each one read out is a channel.
scenes.visual: Most sites dim; a block of 384 stays lit, with the label: read out at once, 384 channels.
scenes.narration: Not necessarily. The original probe reads out only 384 sites at a time. Each one read out is a channel.

scenes.tts: And neurons are not read off sites at all. Software sorts the spikes into units. It can find more units than channels, or fewer.
scenes.visual: Spike waveforms appear on several neighbouring sites, then gather into coloured clusters labelled units.
scenes.narration: And neurons are not read off sites at all. Software sorts the spikes into units. It can find more units than channels, or fewer.

scenes.tts: One neuron shows up on several neighbouring sites. One site hears several neurons.
scenes.visual: One neuron's spike lights three neighbouring sites; then one site is shown picking up spikes from two different neurons.
scenes.narration: One neuron shows up on several neighbouring sites. One site hears several neurons.

scenes.tts: So a unit can merge two neurons, or split one. Treat each unit as an inference, with quality scores.
scenes.visual: Two coloured units fuse into one, then one unit splits into two. A small quality-score badge sits beside each unit.
scenes.narration: So a unit can merge two neurons, or split one. Treat each unit as an inference, with quality scores.

scenes.tts: Notice the ladder. Sites, then channels, then units, then neurons. Each rung is a step from what you want.
scenes.visual: A vertical ladder builds with four rungs labelled sites, channels, units, neurons. A question mark sits on the top rung.
scenes.narration: Notice the ladder. Sites, then channels, then units, then neurons. Each rung is a step from what you want.

scenes.tts: Calcium imaging has a ladder too. A spike lets calcium in, and calcium makes a sensor glow.
scenes.visual: A second ladder beside the first: a sharp spike tick, then a spreading calcium cloud, then a green glow drawn on a much slower time base.
scenes.narration: Calcium imaging has a ladder too. A spike lets calcium in, and calcium makes a sensor glow.

scenes.tts: The glow is real, but it lags and blurs the spike, like steam from a kettle.
scenes.visual: The brief spike tick sits above a slow green hump that rises late and fades slowly. A small kettle icon puffs steam beside it.
scenes.narration: The glow is real, but it lags and blurs the spike, like steam from a kettle.

scenes.visual: The spike tick and the slow green hump hold on screen beside the kettle icon.

scenes.tts: An atlas sorts cells into clusters. Is each cluster a true cell type? Not every one may be.
scenes.visual: A cloud of coloured dots groups into clusters; one cluster carries the label: type?
scenes.narration: An atlas sorts cells into clusters. Is each cluster a true cell type? Not every one may be.

scenes.tts: A connectome counts synapses. Is a count a strength? Treating it as one is an assumption, not a measurement.
scenes.visual: Two neurons joined by a tally of synapse marks; the tally carries the label: strength?
scenes.narration: A connectome counts synapses. Is a count a strength? Treating it as one is an assumption, not a measurement.

scenes.tts: Even a pile of units has a step. Units from one mouse share that mouse.
scenes.visual: The coloured units from the probe slide together and collapse into one mouse icon.
scenes.narration: Even a pile of units has a step. Units from one mouse share that mouse.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea. Each of these numbers is a proxy, one or more steps from your claim.
scenes.visual: A boxed rule begins to build on screen: Each of these numbers is a proxy, one or more steps from your claim.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea. Each of these numbers is a proxy, one or more steps from your claim.

scenes.tts: Name each step. Trust it only as far as someone has measured that step, in conditions like yours.
scenes.visual: The box adds: Name each step. Trust it only as far as it has been measured in conditions like yours.
scenes.narration: Name each step. Trust it only as far as someone has measured that step, in conditions like yours.

scenes.tts: More cells sharpen the estimate for each animal. But they never count as more animals.
scenes.visual: The box adds its last line: more cells sharpen each animal's estimate, but never count as more animals. Beside it, many dots inside one mouse icon, then a row of several mouse icons.
scenes.narration: More cells sharpen the estimate for each animal. But they never count as more animals.

scenes.tts: Every method has a row like this: the number it gives, and the step to your claim.
scenes.visual: A five-row table appears row by row: probe, calcium imaging, any recording, atlas, connectome, with the step for each.
scenes.narration: Every method has a row like this: the number it gives, and the step to your claim.

scenes.tts: The rule says how far to trust a measurement. It cannot show a pathway is needed. That takes a manipulation.
scenes.visual: The table dims. A small caption reads: needed for behaviour? Test with a manipulation.
scenes.narration: The rule says how far to trust a measurement. It cannot show a pathway is needed. That takes a manipulation.

scenes.tts: The next two films follow two of these steps closely: light to spikes, and cells to mice.
scenes.visual: The calcium-imaging row and the any-recording row of the table glow; the others fade.
scenes.narration: The next two films follow two of these steps closely: light to spikes, and cells to mice.
